title: Countable coordinate enlargement invariant under an endomorphism
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $J$ a set and $(N_j)_{j\in J}$ a family of $R$-modules, each countably generated, meaning generated by an at most countable subset. Put $M=\bigoplus_{j\in J}N_j$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. For $A\subseteq J$, write $M_A$ for the coordinate submodule of families supported in $A$ (the support is the set of indices with nonzero coordinate). Let $f:M\to M$ be any $R$-linear endomorphism. For every at most countable subset $C\subseteq J$ there exists an at most countable subset $D\subseteq J$ containing $C$ such that $f(M_D)\subseteq M_D$. No countability hypothesis on $R$ or on the underlying sets of the $N_j$ is imposed.
